title: A 1.10 taxon capture ratio permits both warmth-slope signs for empirical moth dominance in four UK samples in 1992-2015
abstract: We give exact bounds for the largest taxon share when relative capture rates have a fixed ratio limit. We apply the bounds to empirical catches from 685 trap-months in England and Scotland in 1992-2003 and 2004-2015. All four catch warmth slopes are negative, and all four adjusted confidence intervals include zero. A within-month maximum-to-minimum taxon capture ratio of 1.10 permits both slope signs in every sample. Ratios that first permit zero range from 1.004 to 1.041. Explicit capture corrections attain the bounds. Independent linear programs check the formulas. These are fixed-catch sensitivity ranges, not confidence regions for true community composition. Capture rates can vary freely between months. Finite catches, missing taxa, selected samples and coarse weather limit biological inference. Code, source hashes, aggregate results and a figure are included. Record-level data remain external.

display.caption: Catch warmth slopes with four-test confidence intervals, and separate sharp empirical sensitivity ranges at a taxon capture ratio limit of 1.10. The ranges hold observed shares fixed and allow capture corrections to vary freely across months.

citations.reason: Adapt panel build code and reuse the source selection. Raw rebuild matches its verified count and panel tables. Records overlap fully.
Earlier concentration study includes largest-share slopes as a secondary outcome. This study adds exact capture sensitivity bounds.
